svg.text: Mangrove topographic transect: how to measure the profile
Side view (A, vertical scale exaggerated), one segment (B), plan view (C) and the resulting CSV (D). Not to scale.
A · Side view: stations along the tape, from the low-water mark to 5–10 m beyond the 30 m mark
tape distance from the low-water mark (cumulative)
stations (pegs): at every slope change and at most 2 m apart
B · One segment between two stations (dashed box in A): inclination measured on the ground
rigid plastic board (e.g. small whiteboard) lying on the ground
d = slope distance along the tape, station to station
1. Keep the tape taut and straight between the stations.
2. Lay a rigid plastic board flat on the ground along the
tape between the two stations: it keeps the clinometer
out of mud and water and smooths small bumps.
3. Put the clinometer (or phone app) on the board, aligned
with the tape → inclination α (+ uphill landward).
4. Read the cumulative tape distance at the next station.
5. Write both on the field sheet; move to the next segment.
C · Plan view: straight line, one bearing
D · One row per station → CSV for the notebook
• first row: GNSS fix required (lat, lon, z); inclination empty
• inclination = slope of the segment leading to that station
• lat/lon/z on other rows only for optional RTK ties
• handheld GNSS: z approximate; tie to RTK or a benchmark once per site
